standing: AUTHOR candidate for independent review. A finite declarative carrier input for one registry recipe generating crates/contracts/src/generated/protocol.rs and providers/typescript/src/generated/protocol.ts. Not approval, not a production wire decoder, not semantic admission.

ts2-cbor.negativeIntegers: DECODABLE: major type 1 in -2^63..-1 is inside the closed data model; no TS2 carrier member has a negative-integer type, so every negative integer in a TS2 payload refuses as a type mismatch (PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION).
ts2-cbor.mapOrder: ascending bytewise order of each key's deterministic-CBOR encoding
ts2-cbor.frameIntegrity: uint64 big-endian payload length, 32 raw SHA-256 payload bytes, then one canonical-CBOR payload
ts2-cbor.decodeRule: decode once under the host-state-selected closed carrier; re-encode and require byte equality

rust3-cbor.negativeIntegers: FORBIDDEN at decode: any CBOR major type 1 item refuses before carrier typing (rust2 canonicalCbor.forbidden[0]).
rust3-cbor.mapOrder: length of encoded key first, then bytewise
rust3-cbor.frameIntegrity: 8-byte big-endian payload length, 32 raw SHA-256 payload bytes, canonical-CBOR payload (40-byte prefix)
rust3-cbor.decodeRule: retain payload bytes; decode once under the host-state-selected closed carrier; re-encode and require byte equality

profiles.mapOrderEquivalence: For text keys the two map-order rules select the same order: a deterministic-CBOR text key starts with its length header (0x60+n below 24, 0x78 n up to 255, 0x79 nn beyond), so bytewise order of encoded keys is length-first then bytewise. The checker proves it over every carrier member name and random keys.

privateRepresentation.standing: Private carrier choices for one generator recipe; none is a wire change or a wire name.

text.rust: String (NFC and byte bounds checked by admission)

bytes.rust: protocol::wire::ByteString(Vec<u8>) newtype; codec accepts only CBOR major type 2; length prefix checked against maxBytes before allocation
bytes.typescript: Uint8Array (owned copy, never a view into the frame buffer)
bytes.json-vector: lowercase hex in a member named <member>Hex, JSON vectors only; never a JSON array, base64 or hex on the wire and never a generated JSON carrier

null.rust: unit (only inside nullable or variant-record branches)

nullable.rust: Option<T> serialized as present CBOR null; never skipped

optional.rust: Option<T> with skip-when-absent; absent is not null
optional.typescript: prop?: T under exactOptionalPropertyTypes; undefined never serialized

variant-record.rust: enum with one struct per discriminator value; codec writes every memberOrder member including nulls
variant-record.typescript: discriminated union on the discriminator member; every member present

extern.rust: generated type from the registered schema (options.json namespace); JSON-vector integers map to u64/bigint because every extern integer has minimum 0

frame-payload.rust: per-protocol enum; decode entry point takes (frameType, HostSelector) and never tries alternatives
frame-payload.typescript: per-protocol discriminated union with the same selector-parameterized decoder

selectors.negotiated-target-attribution-v2: true iff target-attribution-v2 is in both the admitted Hello and HelloAck token arrays (handshake law factBatch.negotiated)
selectors.host-phase: the host phase in which the Unavailable frame arrives; any other phase has no transition row and faults before payload typing

namespaces.Rust3: rust-provider-protocol.v2 wireSchema successors and native-evidence §9.2 records (this document)
namespaces.extern: Handshake1, Startup1, Native2, Occupancy1 exactly as generator candidate03 options.json names them
namespaces.forbidden: bare CoverageKeyV2, FactCandidateV1, AnchorRefV1, StageResult* or FactBatchV3 type names

orders.sequence: declared order preserved; no sort law beyond the member's admission rules
orders.utf8-strict: strictly ascending by UTF-8 bytes of the text item; duplicates refuse
orders.path-utf8-strict: strictly ascending by UTF-8 bytes of item.path; duplicates refuse
orders.cbor-bytes-strict: strictly ascending by deterministic-CBOR bytes of the item under the language profile; duplicates refuse
orders.cve1-bytes-strict: strictly ascending by CVE1(item) bytes (resolved-inputs.v2 planIdContract.canonicalValueEncoding); duplicates refuse
orders.candidateOrdinal-increasing: candidateOrdinal unique strictly increasing (occupancy vocabulary); each names a candidate of this batch
orders.package-then-path: strictly ascending by (packageKey UTF-8 bytes, path UTF-8 bytes); equals DependencySourceSetV1.packages order then DependencyFileManifestV1 path order
orders.nested-loop-relation-rung-target: rust2 coverageDomainAlgorithm canonical nested-loop order; duplicates refuse
orders.request-order: exactly one item per requested stage, in Analyze request order
orders.outputOrdinal-contiguous: outputOrdinal equals array index; PreparedOutputSetV3.rows order

Ts2ExecutionIdText.note: Startup1ExecutionIdText is minLength 1 only; the exact AttemptRecord value always has this grammar, so a narrower carrier refuses nothing the host constructs.

source.selector: #/$defs/LogicalPath (host constructs manifest paths from the snapshot2 source inventory)

Ts2ProjectPath.note: Normalization/segment law is handwritten admission (d2.snapshotTransport); 4096 is the identity LogicalPath bound of every path the host can construct.

Rust3CanonicalPath.note: rust2 rule (no leading slash, backslash, NUL, drive prefix, empty/dot/dot-dot segment). 4096 bytes is c2 v3 canonicalRelativePath, the bound of every host-constructed path; Native2CanonicalPath is weaker and is not used for this carrier.

Rust3PackageKey.note: Grammar settled by this candidate: name SP version SP sourceId of exactly one DependencySourceSetV1.packages row (same spelling as UnifiedFeaturesV1.activated[].packageKey).

Ts2FrameV2.note: Private name. The wire carries no record name; payload is a nested CBOR map selected by frameType and host state.

Ts2ProviderWorkBudgetV1.note: Inherited shape is any uint64; the host projection emits 1..2^63-1 only (handwritten TS2-BUDGET-PROJECTION).

Ts2StageRequestV1.note: relations keep the C-2 array exactly (already canonical); stageOrdinal is contiguous in this Analyze.

Ts2AnchorRefV1.note: fact-ref stays shape-decodable only so that admission can refuse it with one typed PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION; it never reaches fact2 minting.

Ts2FactBatchV3.note: Wire form of opensip.product.fact-batch.3 for typescript-semantic: candidates carry the CBOR byte string, never the vector hex/decoded pair.

Ts2SnapshotFileSubjectV1.note: Commitment preimage record only; never a frame payload member.

Rust3ProviderFrameV3.note: Private name; RustProviderEnvelopeV2 is not reused and no published name is invented on the wire.

Rust3DependencySourceChunkV3.note: New private record name for an existing frame; member list exactly as §9.2 states. path uses the manifest entry path shape it echoes.

Rust3DependencySourceAcceptedV3.note: Private alias: identical member set and types to Native2DependencySourceSealV3; ACCEPTED-EQUALS-SEAL.

Rust3PreparedOutputEntryV3.note: Member names of PreparedOutputEntryV2 unchanged; value domains substituted to the Plan-bound PreparedOutputSetV3 row (scoped successor SUCC-PREPARED-V3).

Rust3CoverageKeyV2.note: rust2 8-member request key (c2 v3 coverageKey.key). Never merged with Native2CoverageKeyV2 (5-member entry key) or Ts2CoverageKeyV1.

Rust3C2PlanStageV3.note: Optional members are ABSENT (never null) when absent in the ExecutionPlan; deterministic-CBOR(planStage) must equal the selected Plan stage bytes.

Rust3StageResultV2.note: Retained members; values commit CoverageResultV3 (native-evidence §9.7 names StageResultV2.coverageCommitment explicitly).

transitions.overlay: none: T2-14 already guards post-Analyze Unavailable with outputSeen=false; T2-18 keeps Cancel from START (delivery2 cancelTransition).

transitions.precedence: protocol3-transitions.v1.json is the only matching table for major 3; rust2 transitionAstV2 rules are not interpreted. rust2 framePrecheck and the T016/T020 payload guards are retained as pre-match admission (RUST3-FRAME-PRECHECK, DISPATCH-STAGE-CORRELATION, RUST3-BUDGET-EXHAUSTED).
transitions.cancelInStart: No row (P3-29 *PRE_COMPLETE excludes START). The host never emits Cancel before Hello; an interruption in START terminates the child without a Cancel frame and interrupted/130 precedence is unchanged.
transitions.terminalGuards: Unchanged P3 preMatchLaw: FAULT absorbing; any frame after a terminal in WAIT_ZERO_EXIT/WAIT_EOF/DONE faults; process faults from any phase; unmatched frame P3-34.
transitions.custodyOrder: SnapshotAccepted -> DependencySource custody (always) -> PreparedOutput custody iff preparedOutputSetId != null -> NativeContextVerified or pre-Analyze Unavailable -> Analyze (nativeMd §9.1 step 4 lines 2863-2866; P3-08..P3-22).

admission.rule: Declared payload length <= maxFramePayloadBytes 67108864 before allocation; every array/text/byte length checked before allocation. A member with no maxItems/maxBytes is bounded only by this limit.
Envelope protocolMajor == 2 before payload typing.
frameType must belong to the direction being read (closedHostToWorkerFrames + closedWorkerToHostFrames + NativeContextVerified).
Per-direction sequence starts at 0 and increases by exactly 1; overflow refuses.

Before P3 matching: frameType known, direction equals the frame row direction, sequence equals that direction's counter, counter < 2^64-1, payload decodes under the selected carrier with every join below. Failure is FAULT / PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (same outcome as P3-34).
Every snapshotId echo (manifest, chunk, seal, accepted, SubjectScopeV1, AnchorRefV1 source-span, SubjectV2.subjectId preimage) is the exact OpenUniverse snapshot2 text.
Every PreparedOutput{Manifest,Chunk,Seal,Accepted}.planId is the exact OpenUniverse plan2 text.
Analyze executionId/snapshotId/planId (and TS universeKey) equal OpenUniverse.
manifestSha256 = lowercase hex SHA-256(deterministic-CBOR(entries)); no domain, no prefix; Seal and Accepted echo it.
SnapshotManifest, DependencySourceManifest and PreparedOutputManifest manifestSha256 = lowercase hex SHA-256(deterministic-CBOR(entries)); Seal and Accepted echo it.
entries strictly ascending unique by path UTF-8 bytes; kind decides the variant.
file: byteLength uint64, contentSha256 DigestHex, executable bool, targetBytes null; symlink: targetBytes non-empty byte string, other variant members null.

Chunks follow entry order; chunkIndex contiguous from 0 per entry; byteOffset = checked sum of prior chunk bytes; a zero-length entry has no chunk; SHA-256 of the concatenated bytes equals the entry digest; total length equals the entry length.
entryCount = len(entries); total bytes = checked sum of entry lengths (Rust: <= stated limit); totalChunkCount = chunks sent.
Accepted members are exactly the Seal values, after byte/digest/VFS validation.
admission.owner: delivery2 SnapshotAcceptedV1; rust2 SnapshotAcceptedV2; nativeMd §9.2 line 2879

admission.rule: DependencySourceManifestV3.entries ordered package-then-path; each packageKey names one DependencySourceSetV1.packages row by 'name SP version SP sourceId'; the rows of one package are exactly its DependencyFileManifestV1 (H(native.dependency-file-manifest.v1) equals fileManifestSha256; count = fileCount; byte sum = totalBytes); every package of the set appears; entries <= maxDependencySourceEntries; distinct packages <= maxDependencySourcePackages; totalBytes <= maxDependencySourceTotalBytes; chunk bytes <= maxDependencySourceChunkBytes; dependencySourceSetId equals OpenUniverse.repositoryResolution.dependencySourceSetId on every frame. Empty set: entries [], manifestSha256 = hex(SHA-256(0x80)), seal counts 0, no chunk.

entries[i] answers PreparedOutputSetV3.rows[i]: outputOrdinal = i; kind = planRow.kind; planRow = the exact row; logicalPath = '.opensip/prepared/v3/' + i + '-' + planRow.blob.sha256 + '.blob'; blobByteLength/blobSha256 = planRow.blob.byteLength/sha256; contentByteLength/contentSha256 equal the blob values (no V2 wrapper); a generated-file row requires planRow.generated.blob == planRow.blob.

Worker: every planRow.inputBinding.dependencySourceSetId equals repositoryResolution.dependencySourceSetId and cfgSetId names a universe.resolvedInputs.cfgSets entry; row kinds inert only. Host (before spawn): H(native.prepared-output-set.v3, {schemaVersion 3, preparation, rows: [entries[*].planRow]}) == repositoryResolution.preparedOutputSetId; macro-expansion rows <= maxExpansionRows, generated-file rows <= maxGeneratedFileRows, build-script-directives rows <= maxPreparedOutputEntries, totalBlobBytes <= maxPreparedOutputTotalBlobBytes, encoded manifest <= maxFramePayloadBytes; otherwise no spawn (host invariant, operational-failed / SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE as delivery2 coverageDomain.overflowFate).
budget is exactly delivery2 stageRequestProjection.budgetProjection output.
stageRequests are all and only selected stages in verified logical order; stageOrdinal contiguous 0..n-1; dependsOn [] when absent.

stageId is C-2 text (StageIdText) and equals DispatchBindingV1.expectedStageId; stageOrdinal = analyzeRequestOrdinal, never retainedStageOrdinal; FactBatch analysisOrdinal/batchIndex/first candidateOrdinal equal the dispatch expectations; batch count 1..cap (rust2 T016 guard retained as pre-match admission).
admission.owner: dispatch x-opensip-wire.correlation; nativeMd §9.6 lines 3024-3043; rust2 T016

admission.rule: SubjectScopeV1 fully retained: commitment C(opensip.coverage.subject-scope.v1, sorted SnapshotFileSubjectV1[]); subjectCount = kind=file entries; recomputed by host and worker.

Each request key's subjectScopeCommitment = 'sha256:' + hex of scope2 = H('subject-scope', D_key), D_key = {schemaVersion 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse (64-hex suffixes of the key), relation, resolution (the key's), enumeratorClosure (Plan-selected provider closure2 of the stage), subjects (host enumeration)}. Host mints before spawn; the same descriptor drives admit_coverage_result_v3 and pre-Analyze conversion. Worker checks Sha256Text shape only and echoes: entries[i].key.subjectScopeCommitment and entries[i].entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment equal keys[i]. No equality with TS SubjectScopeV1.subjectScopeCommitment or rust2 commitments.subjectScope is required.
domainCommitment = C(opensip.ts-provider.requested-coverage-domain.v1, {subjectScope, keys}); keys carry per-key scope2 values; worker recomputes.
domainCommitment = C(opensip.rust-provider.analysis-domain.v2, {subjects, requestedCoverageDomain}); analysisDomain equals a fresh host reconstruction (wireRule) with per-key scope2 values.
subjectsAlgorithm retained; the snapshotId in the subjectId preimage is the snapshot2 text.
deterministic-CBOR(planStage) equals the selected ExecutionPlan stage bytes; optional members absent exactly when absent.
Universe ids are sha256:hex(H(native.semantic-universe.<language>.v2, universe.resolvedInputs)); CoverageKeyV2 entries carry the 64-hex suffix.
fact-plane candidate law: registry relation/rung/layer/schemaId, producer/language constants, producerVersion = verified providerBuildId, target universe in host-admitted target domain.
canonicalRelationPayload decodes once to the registry payload schema and re-encodes byte-equal; <= 1048576 bytes.

Wire anchor rule (retained fact-plane sourceSpanSchema.rule): source-span requires snapshotId = OpenUniverse snapshot2, path = a kind=file manifest path, contentSha256 = that entry digest, startByte < endByte <= entry byteLength (NON-EMPTY). Array order: TS2 cbor-bytes-strict (delivery2 AnchorRefV1.ordering), Rust3 cve1-bytes-strict (factPlane anchorSchema.ordering); count 1..100000. The shared fact2 rule (identity-model.v3.py line 1892 ANCHOR_RANGE: 0 <= a <= b <= len, plus ANCHOR_UTF8) is NOT narrowed: the non-empty requirement is a provider-wire admission rule only, and zero-length fact2 anchors from other producers stay admissible.

kind=fact-ref is PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION at candidate admission before any fact2 mint, because fact-identity-fact2 is a mandatory identity token in both token sets and identity-schemas.v3 fact.anchors has no fact reference.
occupancyCompanions length <= len(candidates); each candidateOrdinal names a candidate of this batch; targetUniverseId byte-equal to that candidate.
Candidate spool accounting over deterministic-CBOR({analysisOrdinal, stageId, candidate}) retained; bytes budget increments use candidate encoded length.
Every stage/stream/terminal commitment uses exactly the commitmentMap row for its field.
batchCommitment = C(opensip.ts-provider.fact-batch.v1, facts) over wire candidates; FactBatchV3 carries none.
Cancel.executionId is null iff OpenUniverse has not been sent, otherwise its exact value; analysisOrdinal is null iff Analyze has not been sent, otherwise Analyze.analysisOrdinal (TS2: 0).
Cancelled executionId and analysisOrdinal equal the Cancel values.
observedPhase is the inherited enum; snapshot for a Cancel in WAIT_NATIVE_CONTEXT_VERIFIED or READY_ANALYZE.

ProviderFault.executionId/analysisOrdinal: null iff the worker has not received OpenUniverse/Analyze, otherwise the received values; ProviderFault.phase and Cancelled.observedPhase are the host phase in which the Cancel was sent or the fault received (one of the 16 *PRE_COMPLETE phases); detailCode IdentityText, diagnostic only, normalizes to provider-protocol.
triggerStageId = current stage; unit/limit = planStage.budget (a stage without budget or with milliseconds cannot BudgetExhausted); observed = limit + 1 (checked).

commitmentMap.function: C(d, v) = 'sha256:' + lowercase hex SHA-256(UTF8(d) || 0x00 || deterministic-CBOR(v))

rows.value: that stage's entries; equals its Coverage frame value
that stage's wire FactCandidateV1 values in order, whichever FactBatch payload carried them; empty stage commits 0x80

rows.recipe: identity canonical H frame, not DOMAIN_RULE
lowercase hex SHA-256(deterministic-CBOR(entries)); delivery2 commitments.domains.snapshotManifest not applied

commitmentMap.basis: Preimage shape decides the domain: per-stage ordered entries match stageCoverage ('stageCoverageEntries'); stage-major arrays across all requested stages match coverageStream ('stage-major ... values'). Terminal Unavailable/BudgetExhausted coverage is stage-major across all stages, so it is coverageStream. The v1 checker (non-owner, *.v1 domains) used the same structure; the v2 checker executes none of these recipes.
